description: Build, hack, and verify web apps. Find vulnerabilities through red-teaming. Formally verify properties of Rust codes in Lean 4.

written.description: Gives an agent a browser that controls its own network traffic, so the model can capture, edit, replay and compare the requests a web app sends without a proxy in between. Each session runs under a network policy and records every fetch it allowed or refused.

alive.last_commit_message:
browser: decode zstd, store proxy-observed bodies decoded, replay wit… (#729)

* browser: decode zstd, store proxy-observed bodies decoded, replay with the engine's Accept-Encoding

A proxy session stored response bodies as they crossed the wire, so a zstd or
brotli body from Chromium read back as binary, while the store holds decoded
bodies everywhere else. The proxy now decodes them with the engine's decoders
and cap and records the wire encoding and size; a body that does not decode is
kept as received.

A replay of a stored request sent the capturing client's Accept-Encoding,
which for Chromium includes zstd, and the engine then refused the response.
The engine sets the header on a replay unless the caller edits it; raw sends
keep the stored bytes. zstd is decoded (ruzstd, pure Rust) in the engine and
in dom_inject.

* browser proxy: keep relaunched agent-browser proxied, say when capture has gone quiet, name the replay budget fix

The printed start line proxies one agent-browser launch. When its daemon idles
out, a later bare command relaunches an unproxied browser: pages still work and
capture stops without an error. proxy now also prints the environment that
proxies every launch from a shell and points to proxy-open. status shows when
the proxy last let a target request through and warns after five quiet
minutes (refused background traffic does not count).

A replay the session budget refused rendered as an empty answer with an error
line; it is now an error that names --reset-budget.

The docs said Linux trusts only the session CA and needs certutil. proxy passes
--ignore-https-errors on Linux and macOS and does not need certutil; the docs
now say so.

* browser: suggest --no-sandbox when a proxy-open launch is blocked by the sandbox

When `h5i browser proxy-open` fails because Chromium cannot start its sandbox
(no setuid sandbox helper, unusable namespace sandbox), the bail now appends a
hint telling the user to retry with
`AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS=--no-sandbox h5i browser proxy-open <url>` (or the
equivalent agent-browser `--args --no-sandbox`), and notes it disables the
sandbox.

So that retry actually works, the proxy launch flags now merge
AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS into the single `--args` string instead of shadowing it,
while always keeping the loopback bypass. Split out a pure
`agent_browser_proxy_args_with` helper and test the merge and the hint directly.

* docs: regenerate the /manual/ page after the browser manual edits

The earlier browser proxy commit edited docs/MANUAL.md but did not regenerate
the rendered /manual/ page, so the Pages/docs-freshness check failed. Rerun
scripts/gen_manual.py, docs/build-content.py and scripts/stamp_assets.py, and
record the new /manual/ content date and fingerprint in PAGE_HISTORY. sitemap
lastmod follows.
